title: The Tuesday dip
hook: Signup volume drops about 25 percent every single Tuesday and the obvious suspect turns out to be a coincidence.
brief_md:
## Situation

Signup completion volume is noticeably lower on Tuesdays than on any other weekday, and it has been that way for four straight weeks. A checkout-form code deploy shipped on Tuesday, 2026-07-14, and it lines up with one of the dips, which makes it the easy answer.

## Your job

Confirm the dip is real across the full window before naming a cause. Check whether the deploy explanation actually holds on the Tuesdays that had no deploy at all. Watch for two grain problems along the way: payment_attempts joins 1:many against signups, and users.acquisition_channel goes NULL for most of one channel's true volume. Name the real mechanism, and say exactly what evidence would prove your conclusion wrong.

objectives.label: Confirm the Tuesday dip holds across all four weeks, not just one
Avoid the payment_attempts fan-out by aggregating to one row per event_id before joining
Use events.channel instead of users.acquisition_channel to avoid the referral NULL undercount

detector.prompt: Did the learner identify that users.acquisition_channel has a NULL cluster concentrated in the referral channel, and use events.channel as the ground-truth field instead?

objectives.label: Test the code-deploy hypothesis against every Tuesday in the window, not just the one with a deploy

detector.prompt: Did the learner check whether the dip appears on Tuesdays with no code_deploy row, and use that to rule the deploy hypothesis in or out?

objectives.label: State a concrete, checkable condition that would disprove the final conclusion

detector.prompt: Did the learner state a specific, checkable falsification test for their final conclusion, grounded in the data available in this warehouse, rather than a vague or untestable caveat?

verdict_spec.falsifiability_statement: The maintenance-window explanation is falsifiable against this warehouse in two direct ways. First, push and email together drive about 35 percent of signups on every non-Tuesday day of the week (Sunday 35.1%, Monday 35.0%, Wednesday 35.1%, Thursday 35.0%, Friday 34.9%, Saturday 34.8%) but only 14.8 percent on Tuesday; if a future Tuesday without a maintenance_window row showed push+email back at roughly 35 percent of signups, or a future Tuesday with the window still scheduled kept push+email suppressed near 15 percent, the mechanism would be confirmed. If push+email share on a maintenance-window Tuesday came back at the normal ~35 percent instead, the explanation would be disproven. Second, the deploy cross-reference already falsifies the competing explanation: three of the four dipped Tuesdays (2026-06-30, 2026-07-07, 2026-07-21) carry a maintenance_window row and zero code_deploy rows, yet show the same 102-110 signup range as 2026-07-14, which had both. A cause that requires the code deploy cannot explain the dip on those three Tuesdays.
